title: ‘Dhurandhar’ gangster’s brother shot in Karachi
content: Zubair Baloch, brother of jailed gangster Uzair Baloch, was critically wounded in a drive-by shooting. Two masked assailants on a motorcycle opened fire, striking him in the chest and abdomen. Zubair was rushed to Civil Hospital Karachi for emergency surgery after the attack. Police are investigating personal enmity and potential gang war resurgence as motives. The incident occurred in Karachi's Lyari neighborhood, a historic hub of organized crime.

title: Neeraj Chopra takes silver, Yashvir wins bronze as India secure two medals in javelin at CWG
content: Neeraj, the 28-year-old Tokyo Olympic champion, was not at his best in difficult weather but still managed a season-best throw of 85.83m in his second attempt to finish second.

title: PM Modi: I forgive those who abused me & my mom, our job to guide them
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will forgive young protesters accused of abuse. He stated these misguided children need guidance and correction, not punishment. The Prime Minister believes punishing them will not change circumstances effectively. Mistakes made at a young age present an opportunity for correction and societal acceptance. This decision indicates that cases against these youngsters will likely be withdrawn.

title: CWG 2026: India’s finest day in Glasgow yet! Six medals, 10 boxing finalists
content: India produced its biggest day of the 2026 Commonwealth Games, winning six medals to take its tally to 23. Historic judo golds for Asmita Dey and Harsh Singh, athletics medals from Tejaswin Shankar, Neeraj Chopra and Yash Vir Singh, plus a perfect 10-for-10 boxing run into finals highlighted a memorable Day 9 in Glasgow.

title: Amid opposition protest, Lok Sabha passes births & deaths bill
content: The Lok Sabha passed the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Bill, 2026, without any debate. Opposition members disrupted Rajya Sabha proceedings, preventing any business from being transacted. The bill aims to make delayed registrations of births and deaths more stringent. Congress and SP MPs raised issues concerning police actions and alleged temple donation theft. The Rajya Sabha was ultimately adjourned for the entire day.

title: When a district in Florida's Everglades used robot rabbits to eliminate Burmese pythons
content: Florida is employing AI-powered robot rabbits to help locate invasive Burmese pythons. These solar-powered decoys mimic prey using heat and scent to lure snakes. When a python is detected, officials are alerted to remove the invasive species. This technology complements the annual Python Challenge, which has removed thousands of snakes. These efforts aim to control the python population impacting native wildlife.

title: CWG Day 9 medal tally: Where is India now after delivering historic six-medal haul?
content: India enjoyed their best day of the 2026 Commonwealth Games, winning six medals to take their tally to 23. Harsh Singh and Asmita Dey claimed historic judo golds, Neeraj Chopra secured javelin silver, Yash Vir Singh won bronze, Tejaswin Shankar earned India's first decathlon medal, and Yamini Mourya added judo silver as India closed on ninth-placed Wales.

title: Ethanol kept petrol prices lower: Govt
content: Ethanol blending saved consumers nearly thirty rupees per litre on petrol.  Global crude prices reached one hundred thirty-five dollars a barrel recently.  The government kept fuel prices unchanged for seventy-five days initially.  E20 petrol now costs one hundred two rupees per litre in Delhi.  Allegations of foodgrain diversion for ethanol were also rejected.

title: NYC banned Motoclick, now Mamdani targets Uber Eats, DoorDash over 'hidden' tip buttons
content: New York City's delivery workers have gained over one hundred million dollars. This increase follows new rules requiring clear tipping options at checkout. Apps like Uber Eats and DoorDash redesigned their interfaces after city enforcement actions. Workers now see significantly higher hourly earnings and more deliveries completed. The administration continues its efforts to improve app-based worker conditions.

title: 'Project Kusha will cut India’s dependence on imported air shield systems'
content: India successfully tested its indigenous Project Kusha missile system recently. This development aims to create a homegrown long-range air defence capability. The system will counter aerial threats from China and Pakistan effectively. Project Kusha is designed to intercept various aerial targets up to 400 kilometers. Full military induction and deployment are expected between 2028 and 2030.

title: 5 years on, 11 rescued South African elephants thriving in the wild
content: In an inspiring study, South African elephants reintroduced into reserves demonstrated remarkable behavior akin to that of free-roaming herds. Researchers observed that these elephants not only adapted seamlessly to their natural habitats but also maintained optimal stress hormone levels. This research underscores the potential for long-term captive elephants to regain their independence, offering a promising outlook for the conservation efforts throughout southern Africa.

title: US plans $100K fee on foreign students: What it means for engineers
content: The US government is reportedly considering a $100,000 fee for foreign students seeking post-graduation work. This proposed fee targets the Optional Practical Training program, impacting many international graduates.  This follows a significant H-1B visa fee hike imposed on sponsoring companies last year.  Indian engineers, who dominate H-1B approvals, face increased challenges in securing US careers.  The new measures may significantly narrow career paths for many skilled foreign professionals.

title: Chhattisgarh worker shot dead, another wounded in first J&K terror attack on migrants in 21 months
content: Terrorists shot dead a 24-year-old labourer from Chhattisgarh in Kulgam. Another worker from the same state was critically wounded in the attack. Security forces have launched operations to trace the attackers responsible for this incident. This incident marks the first fatal attack on migrant workers since October 18. Officials condemned the attack and directed security forces to intensify operations.

title: 'Jana Nayagan' box office collection: Thalapathy Vijay film drops 12.3%
content: Thalapathy Vijay's Jana Nayagan saw collections drop in its second week. The film earned an estimated 3.55 crore net on its ninth day. Overseas markets contributed 2 crore gross on the same day. Meanwhile, protests in Karnataka led to cancelled screenings at one theatre. The Tamil version continues to be the film's primary revenue generator.

title: Tahir Hussain gets life for IB staffer’s killing in 2020 riots
content: A Delhi court sentenced former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain and four others to life imprisonment.  They were convicted for the murder of Intelligence Bureau staffer Ankit Sharma.  The court found Sharma was lynched solely on account of his religion during the 2020 riots.  While the prosecution sought the death penalty, it was declined by the judge.  The judge considered educational backgrounds as a mitigating factor for the convicts.

title: How family tragedy shaped Lamine Yamal's remarkable journey to football stardom
content: Lamine Yamal's rise to winning the 2026 FIFA World Cup is inseparable from the story of the family that built him. His mother Sheila Ebana was 16 when she gave birth to him. His father Mounir, a Moroccan immigrant, worked construction and street jobs to stay afloat. His grandmother Fátima crossed from Morocco to Spain alone, undocumented, and worked three jobs to bring her children over. His father survived a life-threatening stabbing in August 2024. Yamal's name itself honours two strangers who helped his parents financially before he was born. This is the full human story behind the boy who hugged his little brother on a World Cup pitch in New Jersey.

title: Nolan Wells case takes shocking turn as California man arrested after death
content: It has been close to a month since Nolan Wells died tragically. While authorities investigate his case, a man has now been arrested for a different reason.

title: Brittany Mahomes breaks silence on women eyeing Chiefs star Patrick Mahomes
content: Patrick Mahomes and his wife Brittany Mahomes have been together for close to two decades now but it seems the attention has also sparked women pursuing the star player. The popular entrepreneur brittany Mahomes has now opened up about women pursuing her husband.

title: Cybercriminals widen net as assessees rush to meet I-T return filing deadline
content: Cybercriminals are targeting taxpayers during income tax return filing season. They send fake notices via WhatsApp and use cloned tax portals. These scams aim to steal banking credentials and gain device access. Attackers use malware-laden attachments and phishing websites to deceive victims. This campaign exploits the expectation of official communications from the tax department.

title: 16.4% deleted in Haryana draft roll; 10.8% in Andhra Pradesh
content: Draft voter rolls in Haryana and Andhra Pradesh reveal significant exclusions.  Over sixteen percent of Haryana's electorate and over ten percent in Andhra were removed.  Reasons cited include deaths, permanent shifts, and multiple registrations.  However, genuine voters can still be added during the claims period.  This process allows for corrections and additions to the electoral rolls.

title: Gold loans jump 94% y-o-y, fuel bank credit growth in Q1
content: Gold loans fueled a significant acceleration in bank credit during Q1FY27. This segment expanded by 93.8% year on year, adding substantial value. Overall bank credit also saw robust growth, crossing a significant milestone. Credit to industry recorded its highest first-quarter expansion in recent years. Vehicle loans and medium enterprises also showed strong performance.

title: Monsoon likely to be ‘below normal’ in Aug-Sept: IMD
content: India's monsoon rainfall is expected to be below normal during August and September. This forecast is influenced by the continuing risk of El Niño, which often weakens the monsoon. July rainfall, however, turned out to be normal due to plentiful showers in central India. These showers helped reduce the overall monsoon rainfall deficit significantly by the end of July.

title: 'Pak-trained Mujahideen turned guns inwards': MEA slams Islamabad over PoK crackdown
content: India condemned Pakistan's admission of training and arming militants who have turned against the state. The Ministry of External Affairs also criticized Pakistan's harsh crackdown on protesters in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir. Over forty civilians were reportedly killed during the violent suppression of peaceful demonstrations. India stated that Pakistan's actions exposed its disdain for the region's innocent inhabitants.

title: SC slaps Rs 1 lakh fine on Rajasthan government for harassing official
content: The Supreme Court has ordered Rajasthan to pay one lakh rupees to a government official. This payment is compensation for harassment caused by political interference in a prosecution sanction. The court criticized the joint secretary of the former chief minister for undue influence. Such interference was deemed a blatant display of political dictate by the state. The official was unnecessarily dragged to court, prompting the court's strong observations.

title: Jharkhand zoo hatches cobra and sand boa eggs through artificial incubation first time
content: The Bhagwan Birsa Biological Park successfully incubated Spectacled Cobra eggs artificially. Five healthy hatchlings emerged after a seventy-day incubation period under controlled conditions. The park also welcomed eight Sand Boa hatchlings during this conservation initiative. This success highlights the importance of scientific management in reptile breeding programs. The hatchlings are now under close observation and veterinary care.

title: CWG: India strike double gold in judo as Asmita Dey, Harsh Singh make history
content: Asmita created history by becoming the first Indian judoka to win a Commonwealth Games gold medal after defeating Canada's Heidi Quach in the women's 48kg final.

title: Hockey jersey row: Dilip Tirkey questions process, his federation cites precedent
content: Hockey India president Dilip Tirkey questioned the jersey colour change process.  He stated the decision lacked executive board discussion and his prior knowledge.  Executive director RK Srivastava defended the saffron kit based on technical and performance factors.  Other board members also raised concerns about transparency and accountability.  This controversy emerges amid ongoing governance scrutiny for Hockey India.

title: 'I felt that everything was over': Asmita remembers late father after historic judo gold
content: Asmita Dey secured India's first judo gold medal at the Commonwealth Games. She defeated Canada's Heidi Quach in a gripping golden score final match. This historic victory came after overcoming personal tragedy and immense dedication. Harsh Singh also won a gold medal in the men's 60kg judo event. These twin triumphs marked a significant breakthrough for Indian judo.

title: MAGA piles on to Morocco as Trump twits Spain over Ceuta
content: The migrant surge into Ceuta is escalating into a geopolitical flashpoint. President Trump is using the crisis to reinforce his border security message. This event is also fueling online conspiracy theories linking it to wider international disputes. US officials have intervened in Spain's domestic politics regarding immigration policies. The situation highlights strained US-Spain relations and territorial claims over Ceuta.

title: Heaps of cash & gold, 242 vehicles & more: WB CM Suvendu lists Tulu Mondal's assets
content: Authorities have confiscated more than Rs 150 crore in cash, gold, and various assets belonging to mining mogul Tulu Mondal. This haul comprises numerous vehicles, petrol pumps, and several properties. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari attributed the rise of this illegal operation to the former Chief Minister, claiming that illegal stone mining led to a staggering Rs 15,000 crore revenue loss over a stretch of fifteen years.

title: Tough road for Trump: Why sanctions Bill for tariffs on Russian oil buyers may fail
content: Lawmakers from both parties, along with industry trade groups, have raised concerns over a section of the legislation that would allow Trump to impose hefty tariffs on countries that buy significant volumes of Russian oil and gas.

title: Rashmika Mandanna suffers major hip injury on set; doctors advise six weeks of rest
content: Actress Rashmika Mandanna sustained a major hip injury while filming an intense dance sequence. Doctors have advised her a complete rest period of six weeks for recovery. This injury will likely impact her ongoing film schedules and endorsement commitments. Mandanna is currently working on several big-budget films and numerous brand endorsements. Fans are sending well wishes for her swift return to full fitness.

title: Mukesh Khanna says CJP doesn't represent students or Gen Z
content: Veteran actor Mukesh Khanna has weighed in on the ongoing controversy surrounding the recent Gen Z protests, reacting to the self-styled Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and backing criticism over the alleged use of abusive language against Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The actor described some protesters as "cockroaches" and alleged that they did not represent genuine students.

title: Perfect 5-0! Indian boxers storm into CWG finals after dominant semifinal sweep
content: India's boxing contingent achieved a flawless 5-0 record in the semifinals. Five Indian boxers have now secured spots in the gold medal bouts. Arundhati Choudhary defeated the defending champion in a significant upset victory. Jaismine Lamboria and Preeti Pawar also advanced with dominant performances. Ankush Panghal and Jadumani Singh completed the perfect sweep for India.

title: ‘Samudra Manthan’: Cabinet approves Rs 84,084 cr scheme for oil & gas exploration
content: The scheme will be implemented through FY2030-31 with an aim to harness India's vast offshore energy resources - in what the government has termed as a modern day Samudra Manthan.

title: 'Clarify algorithmic bias': Govt summons Meta's global team over PM Modi post
content: India's government has summoned Meta's global team to discuss Prime Minister Modi's post. Officials will question the social media giant on algorithmic bias and content moderation. Meta's global representatives will also appear before a parliamentary panel for scrutiny. Hyderabad police have also registered cases against Meta India's head. This marks an escalation in the government's oversight of the company's practices.

title: Railway Tracks Washed Away, Severely Damaged Amid Assam Floods
content: Assam Floods: Railway tracks were washed away due to which rail services had been hit in a major way under Tinsukia Railway division of North East Frontier Railway.

title: Strengthening El Nino "Adding Fuel To A Planet Already On Fire": UN Chief
content: A strengthening El Nino that could shatter all-time records is "adding fuel to a planet already on fire" and pushing the world into "uncharted territory," UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres warned Friday.

title: Trump Orders Iran Strikes As Soon As This Weekend: Report
content: US President Donald Trump has instructed the military to execute a fresh assault against Iran as early as this weekend, according to a Wall Street Journal report published Friday.

title: Kartarpur Corridor To Remain Shut Over Security Concerns: Centre
content: The Centre has received representations from Sikh religious groups and organisations for "early reopening" of the Sri Kartarpur Sahib Corridor, but the extant security scenario compels the corridor to "remain suspended".

title: Trump Says US Has Not Agreed To Ukraine Building Patriot Missiles
content: President Donald Trump said on Friday that the United States has not agreed to Ukraine building Patriot missiles but that talks are ongoing, adding that the US must be "very careful about letting somebody build them."

title: US Immigration Agent Arrests Johns Hopkins Researcher At Airport
content: US immigration agents arrested a Johns Hopkins University researcher at an airport where she planned to board a domestic flight.

title: Government Likely To Introduce Foreign Funding Amendment Bill Next Week
content: The government is likely to introduce 'Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act Amendment Bill' in the Lok Sabha next week, sources said.

title: US, Israel Planning To Bombard Energy-Related Targets In Iran: Report
content: The US and Israel are planning a bombing campaign against energy infrastructure targets in Iran, with strikes possible throughout the weekend, CBS News reported on Friday, citing sources.

title: Stopped India-Pak War During Operation Sindoor With Tariff Threat: Trump
content: New Delhi has consistently disputed Trump's claims regarding the loss of 11 aircraft during the engagement while remaining steadfast in rejecting any external mediation.

title: US Fighter Jet Crashes Near California Military Base
content: A US F-35 fighter jet crashed Friday near a military base in San Diego, but the pilot was able to eject before impact, officials said.

title: Russian Grain Lobby Says Kyiv's Attacks Threaten Black Sea Exports
content: Russia, the world's largest wheat exporter, and Ukraine, also a major agricultural exporter, have been attacking each other's agricultural export facilities and commercial vessels in the Black Sea area in recent weeks.

title: For Pak, Kashmir Terror Attack A Ruse To Divert Attention From PoK: Experts
content: Preliminary reports say the Resistance Front (TRF), an off-shoot of Pakistan based Lashkar-i-Toiba (LeT) is believed to be behind the attack.

title: 4 Mountaineers Killed, 6 Missing After Avalanche Strikes Peak In PoK
content: The avalanche struck the mountain at an altitude of around 7,000 metres Thursday, sweeping away the 10-member climbing team that had begun its summit push, according to the Alpine Club of Pakistan (ACP).

title: Italy Suspends Schengen Agreement With Spain Because Of Ceuta Migrant Crisis
content: On Thursday, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni called for Spain to be suspended from the Schengen area, describing the images from Ceuta showing thousands of arriving migrants as "shocking".

title: 57 Dead, 60,000 Enter From Morocco: All About Crisis In Spain's Enclave Ceuta
content: Spain's interior ministry claimed that half of the migrants had already gone back to Morocco, sharing footage of people walking back through a fence door at the border.

title: Uzair Baloch's Brother Shot Multiple Times In Karachi's Lyari By Unknown Gunmen
content: According to a statement issued by Chakiwara police, the 40-year-old was shot on main Chakiwara Road. The two injured bystanders were shifted along with him to Civil Hospital Karachi for treatment.

title: 'Want To Forgive Them': PM Modi On Students Who Abused Him at Jantar Mantar
content: In a video message, PM Modi referred to the events at Jantar Mantar, where a section of protesters allegedly used expletives against him and his late mother.

title: 32 Killed In Pak After Coal Mine Explosion Near Quetta
content: Rescue teams have recovered 32 bodies overnight from two coal mines in the Sorange coalfield near Quetta after a methane gas explosion, while search operations remain underway to find two more miners, according to a report by Dawn citing an official.

title: After Akali Dal, Sacrilege Row Engulfs Bhagwant Mann Government
content: From contributing to the end of Shiromani Akali Dal's dominance after the 2015 incidents to becoming a recurring electoral litmus test for successive governments, the issue of sacrilege has repeatedly reshaped the state's political landscape.

title: Delayed aid, prolonged ordeal
content: For tuberculosis (TB) patients from economically backward regions, financial assistance through government initiatives is as crucial as medication. Delays in disbursing aid are affecting the recovery of patients from across Andhra Pradesh as they struggle to afford nutritious food and travel for treatment, writes Nellore Sravani

content: The Karnataka Mango Development and Marketing Corporation will develop a dedicated platform to facilitate the sale of Alphonso mangoes in the domestic market.

title: Let the ink flow: Collectors and craftsmen keep fountain pens alive in Hyderabad
content: At the Hyderabad Fountain Pen Club’s monthly gatherings, collectors, hobbyists and craftsmen come together to share pens, inks and paper, exchange stories and celebrate the art of handwriting. Their passion is complemented by the work of veteran city penmakers who continue to handcraft ebonite fountain pens using time-honoured techniques, keeping alive a tradition that has endured well into the digital age

title: Villagers demand operation of overhead tank for regular water supply in Tiruvannamalai
content: Residents travel at least 5-10 km to fetch a few pots of water from Kilpennathur and Tiruvannamalai towns due to irregular water supply

title: A genetic blueprint for saving Asia’s iconic hornbills
content: A new study by researchers from CCMB-Hyderabad, and the Nature Conservation Foundation- Mysore has decoded the complete genomes of four species, offering fresh insights into their evolution and population history over millions of years. The findings reveal how past climatic shifts shaped hornbill populations and provide valuable genetic resources to guide conservation strategies for these ecologically important seed dispersers

title: PM Modi, Burnham discuss trade pact in 1st call
content:
NEW DELHI: Congratulating UK PM Andy Burnham on assuming office, PM Narendra Modi said the two leaders will collaborate closely to fully harness the trade and investment opportunities presented by the recently operationalised India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), for the "shared prosperity and well-being of both our people". Burnham officially took office as UK PM on July 20, 2026. The leaders discussed the West Asia conflict, agreeing to continue to work closely together towards de-escalation and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. According to the UK, Burnham set out his ambitions to further enhance ties, including through the UK-India Vision 2035 framework.

title: US proposes stricter J-1 visa rules; Indian researchers, docs could be affected
content: Lubna Kably is a senior editor, who focuses on various policies and legislation. In particular, she writes extensively on immigration and tax policies. The Indian diaspora is the largest in the world; through her articles she demystifies the immigration-policy related developments in select countries for outbound students, job aspirants and employees.
